clue.text: Larval protection that can yield fit sprog?

indicators.note: the following words can be made to yield something else by rearranging what they are made of

parts.note: the letters of a healthy child, taken as written

explanation.surface: Something that protects a larva and might produce a healthy little child.
explanation.walkthrough: A sprog is British slang for a small child. Frogspit, also called cuckoo spit, is the froth a froghopper nymph hides in.
explanation.definitionFit: The froth surrounds and shields the froghopper's larva while it feeds, so it is literally a larval shelter.

clue.text: In local speech 'truly' say is replacing US for 'howdy-do'

indicators.note: one item is put in place of another within a word, as a stand-in takes over a post

parts.note: a howdy-do is a fuss or commotion
say means for example, abbreviated eg
taken as written, the letters to be swapped out

explanation.surface: A dialect note on how locals say 'truly', using a US expression.
explanation.walkthrough: Take FUSS and put EG where its US was, giving FEGS, a Scots exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Fegs is a Scots and dialect interjection meaning in faith or truly, hence regional speech.

clue.text: Foreign pick-up in novel for store's delivery guy

indicators.note: one thing sits within the other, so these letters go inside the novel

parts.note: a roman is a novel, as in roman à clef
a ute is an Australian pick-up truck

explanation.surface: An imported pick-up truck appears in a novel about a shop's delivery driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign' signals that the pick-up is the Australian UTE; roman is the French-derived word for a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A routeman is a salesman or deliverer who travels a fixed round for a shop or firm.

clue.text: Ramp maybe, one with leg on each side

parts.note: the leg side in cricket is also called the on side
the Roman numeral for one
the same on side repeated, so one is flanked by it

explanation.surface: A ramp has one leg on either side, like a trestle.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the leg side of the field is also called the on side. A ramp is the wild leek (ramson), a member of the onion family, so it is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramps are wild alliums of the onion genus, so a ramp is one kind of wild onion.

clue.text: Grand girl in novel accompanying knight, an old fellow

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand
Emma is Jane Austen's heroine and title of her novel
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A grand young woman in a novel walks beside a knight who is old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accompanying' simply sets the knight's letter after the girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemman is an old colloquial contraction of gentleman, so it names a man or fellow.

clue.text: Cancel sleep, being restless and losing colour

indicators.note: something restless will not stay still, so the letters before it move about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who skips sleep is restless and grows pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Pallescence is the process of growing pale, so it is a fading or loss of colour.

clue.text: Spicy dish cheers man

parts.note: ta is British informal thanks, like cheers
a man is a male

explanation.surface: Raising a toast to a hot meal: cheers, man!
explanation.definitionFit: A tamale is a Mexican food of seasoned meat in maize dough steamed in a husk.

clue.text: Country swell enveloped by compliments

indicators.note: the answer is wrapped inside the next word, as a letter in an envelope

parts.note: the inner run of letters of this word

explanation.surface: A rural dandy is showered with flattery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell' looks like a fashionable man; here it is the verb meaning to fill out, and 'Country' marks it as dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Plim is a dialect verb meaning to swell or fill out, as wood does when wet.

clue.text: Flat design artist's come up with

parts.note: a plan is a design

indicators.note: in a down light, coming up means the letters climb, so they read from bottom to top

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: An artist has thought up a design that is flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Planar means lying in a single plane, that is, two-dimensional and level.

clue.text: Pils? that's about it for those nicking what's not theirs!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pilsner, a pale beer

definitions.text: for those nicking what's not theirs
definitions.meaning: second meaning: to lag is slang for to steal, so one who lags would be a thief

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: Chambers gives lag as slang for steal, so the word read as lag-er describes a thief. The 'that's about it' phrasing points at that wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Pils is short for pilsner, the classic pale bottom-fermented beer of the lager family.

clue.text: Suitable for regular traffic? Hard to believe in grassland, we hear

indicators.note: one item goes within the other, the claim set inside the grassland
what we hear is a word sounded out, so its spelling is replaced by a matching sound

parts.note: a mead is a meadow, spoken the same as meed, a reward
a tall story is hard to believe

explanation.surface: Something unbelievable is said to be going on in a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: A metalled road has a hard surface of broken stone, ready for everyday vehicles.

clue.text: Enzyme regrettably consumed in viand

indicators.note: what is consumed ends up inside the eater, so these letters go within the food

parts.note: a cate is a dainty or item of food
alas expresses regret

explanation.surface: A digestive enzyme has sadly been eaten along with a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Catalase is the enzyme that breaks down hydrogen peroxide into water and oxygen in living cells.

clue.text: Drunk, one in cling uncomfortably showing effect of corsetry

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk

indicators.note: one item sits within the next word's letters
things lying uncomfortably shift about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a means one

explanation.surface: A tipsy person is squeezed awkwardly into a clinging garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Tightlacing is the practice of lacing stays very tightly, giving the narrow waist a corset produces.

clue.text: Coarse thread I used to join parts of fish with hands in Scotland

indicators.note: something that joins two parts sits between them, so the letter splits the word in two

parts.note: gump is Scots for to catch fish by groping with the hands
taken as written

explanation.surface: A thick cord serves to tie together pieces of fish caught barehanded north of the border.
explanation.definitionFit: Guimp is a variant of gimp, a cord or coarse thread used for trimming and lacemaking.

clue.text: Ape in perfect condition, with dull coating

indicators.note: a coating surrounds what it covers, so these letters wrap round the rest

parts.note: matt or mat means without shine
go as an adjective means in good working order, as in all systems go

explanation.surface: A monkey in fine fettle has a lacklustre coat.
explanation.definitionFit: The magot is the Barbary macaque, the tailless monkey of North Africa and Gibraltar.

clue.text: Body opening's almost repaired

indicators.note: what is repaired has been worked on and put back in a new state, so the letters are reorganised

parts.note: taken as written, not as a shortening signal

explanation.surface: A hole in the body has nearly been mended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' looks like a signal to drop a letter, but every letter of it is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Stomal is the adjective from stoma, a mouth-like pore or surgical opening, so it means relating to one.

clue.text: Deity reversing a hindrance with injection of energy

indicators.note: turning something round to face the other way, so the letters run backwards
an injection puts something inside, so a letter goes into the middle

parts.note: a snag is a hindrance
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A god turns back an obstacle, given a boost of vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Ganesa (Ganesh) is the elephant-headed Hindu god, remover of obstacles.

clue.text: High card following lower one? It may facilitate finesse

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the high card is placed behind the lower one rather than in clue order

parts.note: a ten is a lower card
the ace is the top card

explanation.surface: A card-player's question about playing a top card after a smaller one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts the high card after the lower one. In bridge or whist a tenace is two cards like ace-queen, with a gap where the king should be.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding a tenace lets a player try a finesse, playing the lower card hoping the missing middle one lies favourably.

clue.text: Forming braids, special, in ringlets, not left plaited

indicators.note: plaited strands are woven over each other, so the letters interlace in a new order
without the left, the letter standing for that side is removed

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for special
taken as written; L for left is then dropped

explanation.surface: A hairdresser works special curls into plaits without leaving any loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Tressing is arranging hair in tresses, that is, plaiting it into braids.

clue.text: Reckless conspirator, name associated with mutiny, fired up inside

indicators.note: this part is placed within the other word

parts.note: The Caine Mutiny is Herman Wouk's novel

indicators.note: in a down light, up means the letters read from the bottom upward

parts.note: lit means set on fire

explanation.surface: A rash plotter's name is linked with a rebellion that got heated.
explanation.definitionFit: Catiline was the Roman noble whose reckless plot against the Republic Cicero exposed in 63 BC.

clue.text: Solitary flower framed by mullion

indicators.note: a frame encloses a picture, so these letters sit within the next word

parts.note: monial is an old word for a mullion
the aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: A single bloom is seen through a mullioned window.
explanation.definitionFit: Monasterial means relating to a monastery, the cloistered life of those living apart from the world.

clue.text: Primitive latrine converted from chalet store

indicators.note: something converted is made over into a different form, so the letters are rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rough toilet made by converting a hut's storeroom.
explanation.definitionFit: An earth closet is a lavatory where dry earth, not water, covers waste: a basic outdoor privy.

clue.text: More than one such will be bundled up in harvest

definitions.text: More than one such will be bundled up in harvest

parts.words: More than one such will be bundled up in harvest
parts.note: surface reading: sheaves of corn tied together at harvest time
setter's reading: the plural of the answer, its letters jumbled, spells harvest

explanation.walkthrough: A thrave is a measure of sheaves, so several are indeed bundled at harvest; add S to make the plural and those seven letters rearrange into HARVEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrave is a Scots and northern measure of twenty-four sheaves of corn, gathered in the reaping.

clue.text: Unknown in the Underworld, we're always to be seen in the Bull

definitions.text: we're always to be seen in the Bull

indicators.note: one item placed within the other, the letter inside the realm

parts.note: Hades is the Greek underworld
y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Lost souls in Hades insist they are forever visible within a bull.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks as the stars themselves: 'we' are a cluster always seen in Taurus.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hyades are a star cluster in the head of Taurus, the constellation of the Bull.

clue.text: Local swell tutors delinquent

indicators.note: a delinquent strays from good order, so the letters are misbehaving and out of place

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A local toff gives lessons to young offenders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell' is the verb, and 'Local' flags dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Strout is a dialect verb meaning to bulge or puff out.

clue.text: It looks to have been wet, making love in the mud

definitions.text: It looks to have been wet

indicators.note: one item placed within the other, the round letter set inside the muck

parts.note: mire is mud
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Lovers in the mud end up looking soaked.
explanation.definitionFit: Moiré is watered silk, fabric finished with a rippled sheen that looks like water marks.

clue.text: Girl suggesting divine beauty, mostly in the saddle?

indicators.note: most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: riding sits astride the horse

explanation.surface: A lovely girl on horseback, looking almost heavenly.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrid is a Scandinavian girl's name usually glossed as divine beauty.

clue.text: Some bread, but no banger

explanation.walkthrough: A banger is British slang for a sausage, which fits the bread, but here it means an old rattling car. Rolls is short for a Rolls-Royce, the opposite of a banger.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rolls-Royce, informally a Rolls, is a byword for luxury motoring, never a decrepit old car.

clue.text: Navigation system one introduced cut short

indicators.note: something introduced is brought inside, so the letter goes into the next word

parts.note: shorn means clipped close
a means one

explanation.surface: One navigation system was brought in and then cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoran, from short-range navigation, is a radar system fixing position by signals from two ground stations.

clue.text: Scholar scribbled bit of Homer out in cloistered studies

indicators.note: scribbled writing is jumbled and hard to read, so the letters get mixed up
out means removed, so the named letter is taken away

parts.note: taken as written
the opening letter of the poet's name is to be removed

explanation.surface: A scholar in a cloister scrawled notes on Homer.
explanation.definitionFit: A carol, also carrel, is a small enclosed study nook in a monastery cloister or library.

clue.text: Letter from Tel Aviv date shown in unsealed enclosure?

indicators.note: displayed within, so the letter sits inside the envelope

parts.note: an SAE, stamped addressed envelope, is enclosed with a letter and left unsealed
D is the abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: A letter from Israel carries a date inside an open envelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' looks like correspondence, but it is an alphabet letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sade or tsade is a letter of the Hebrew alphabet, the language of Tel Aviv.

clue.text: House I got back? it's a long story

indicators.note: getting something back returns it the other way, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: the Dáil is the lower house of the Irish parliament
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone recovers their house and starts telling the tale.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iliad is Homer's epic of the Trojan war, a very long narrative poem.

clue.text: What'll start falling off limes in autumn?

definitions.text: What'll start falling off limes in autumn?

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are what count, so only their first letters are kept

parts.note: the opening letters of the five words

explanation.surface: What drops from lime trees each autumn?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: lime trees shed their leaves in autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: Folia is the plural of folium, Latin for a leaf, so it means leaves.

clue.text: Sensitive spot? Dr even puzzled about English name (8, two words)

indicators.note: going round something, so the jumble wraps the next letters
puzzled means confused, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Even the doctor was baffled by an English name.
explanation.definitionFit: A nerve ending is where a nerve fibre terminates and detects stimuli, the body's sensitive point.

clue.text: What Scots do if cross-eyed? or goggle-eyed in part

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is needed, a run of its letters

parts.note: a run straddling the hyphen

explanation.surface: Asking how cross-eyed or bug-eyed Scots behave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glee' suggests joy, but in Scots it is a verb, to squint.
explanation.definitionFit: Glee or gley is Scots for to squint, which is what a person with a cast in one eye does.

clue.text: Following foreign gent, these excited rubberneck?

parts.note: Sig. abbreviates the Italian signor

indicators.note: excited things are stirred up, so the letters move about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: These excited tourists trail after an overseas gentleman to stare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' sets the jumble after the Italian gent's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To rubberneck is to gawp about like a tourist, so as a verb it means go sightseeing.
